analysis.evidence: נֹחַ names Noah as the one who awoke, and מִיֵּינוֹ identifies the condition he woke from, his wine-induced stupor. The next verb, וַיֵּדַע, recounts what he learned on waking.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject נֹחַ.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּיקֶץ נֹחַ מִיֵּינוֹ, “Noah awoke from his wine,” נֹחַ names the subject of וַיִּיקֶץ. The same subject continues with וַיֵּדַע, “and he knew.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּיקֶץ נֹחַ מִיֵּינוֹ means “Noah awoke from his wine.” The verb “awoke” shows that the wine is in view through its intoxicating effect on Noah.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן means “from.” Its נ assimilates to the initial י of the masculine singular construct noun יֵין. The third-person masculine singular suffix וֹ means “his” and refers to Noah.

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:24 as evidence for the affected person under the existing Hebrew sense le-dative.
draft.definition: לְ marks the person to whom something is done.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:24 uses עָשָׂה לוֹ for what Noah’s younger son had done to him.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לוֹ בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן, “what his younger son had done to him,” בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן names the son as the one who acted, and לוֹ identifies Noah as the one affected.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ takes the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix וֹ, referring to Noah.
analysis.sense: Marks the person affected by an action.

draft.change: Add the age sense of קָטֹן to the existing adjective.
draft.definition: Younger or youngest in relation to others in a family or group.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:24 uses הַקָּטָן after בְּנוֹ to identify Noah’s son by relative age.

analysis.evidence: In בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן, “his youngest son,” the adjective identifies which of Noah’s sons did what Noah learned about when he awoke. The comparison concerns the son’s age among his brothers.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute adjective. The adjective agrees in gender, number, and definiteness with בְּנוֹ, “his son,” which is definite through its possessive suffix.
